summary.oneLiner: Flomic Global Logistics operates a lean, asset-light 3PL model focused on freight forwarding and warehousing for SMEs in India. Its credit profile reflects modest scale and stable but limited financial buffers, with a BBB- rating indicating moderate credit risk.

hero.oneLiner: Flomic Global Logistics operates a lean, asset-light 3PL model focused on freight forwarding and warehousing for SMEs in India. Its credit profile reflects modest scale and stable but limited financial buffers, with a BBB- rating indicating moderate credit risk.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- 38+ years of legacy as an integrated, asset-light logistics platform spanning Air, Sea, Land and Specialized Logistics, serving 5,000+ active customers across SME and enterprise segments via a PAN-India network of 30 branches and 30+ warehouses.
- Strong promoter ownership (~69%) and a CRISIL BBB-/Stable rating, alongside a diversified customer base with no single-customer concentration risk: top 15 customers contribute only 20% of turnover and 51% of business is repeat.
- Grew from a regional Mangalore operator founded in 1988 to a BSE-listed (2020) global freight-forwarding player, entering warehousing, event logistics, courier and transportation verticals over 2018-2026.
- Cited competitive strengths: asset-light and scalable model, technology-integrated operations, pan-India physical presence with global partner network, and disciplined working-capital efficiency.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Rs.43 Crore Cash Credit (core working capital); Rs.2 Crore Bank Guarantee (trade-related)

guidance.title: Guidance / outlook
guidance.body: No explicit guidance provided; rating outlook stable based on current operational and financial profile

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: No disclosed expansion plans or new service lines

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: High reliance on single bank (ICICI); limited financial transparency; small scale exposes to client concentration risk; no public financial statements to verify profitability

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The Rs.45 Cr loan facility is entirely from ICICI Bank — indicating extreme banking concentration, which is a hidden liquidity risk if credit lines are tightened

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body: - [Industry] India's logistics cost has fallen to 7.97% of GDP; the deck frames policy reform and digital integration as tailwinds that will lift outsourcing and freight volumes and favour integrated players like Flomic.
